ops.title: v14 accepted divergence: non-UTF-8 paths are loud-error beyond discovery (P6 contract docs)
ops.body:
FIX E adjudication (P4 finder pass, team-lead decision 2026-07-16): the discovery boundary converts paths as PathBuf both directions (rust/crates/py/src/discovery.rs), so surrogate-escaped (non-UTF-8) paths survive discovery — inputs no longer raise UnicodeEncodeError at the &str conversion, and returned paths are real pathlib.Path objects, never to_string_lossy-corrupted strings.

ACCEPTED, REPRESENTATION-BLOCKED DIVERGENCE for every other native path boundary: stream_parse / session_activity_probe / activity_lift / query_session / tool_facts (python.rs), WatchTailer.tick roots and returned rows (watch.rs), and the corrections db path (corrections.rs) still take String — a surrogate path fed to them raises a LOUD UnicodeEncodeError naming the boundary. So discovery can now RETURN a surrogate path that a downstream boundary loudly rejects; that is strictly better than the prior state (silent path corruption at discovery output), and matches house style: crash on the unexpected, never corrupt silently. The full ~15-signature PathBuf sweep was considered and REJECTED: Claude Code writes UUID-named transcripts (never-occur input in practice), and macOS APFS cannot even materialize non-UTF-8 filenames, so the scenario is Linux-only.

For the P6 contract docs: document that non-UTF-8 transcript paths are supported through discovery and rejected loudly at parse/watch/activity/corrections boundaries. Regression pin: tests/test_discovery.py::test_surrogate_escaped_paths_cross_the_boundary (input half; the on-disk output half is unprovable on APFS and rides the same PathBuf conversion).
